scale_note: Manages across all major Austin neighborhoods; handles the city licensing process for its managed properties
angle: Strongest single angle on this list. They are already walking clients through the July 1 2026 licensing requirement. Every property they re-license is a listing being rebuilt — and the occupancy-cap change means the photos and the advertised capacity may no longer agree.
verified: Live (403 to curl — Cloudflare bot protection, site is up)

scale_note: Locally owned full-service: listing on Airbnb and VRBO, check-in/out, housekeeping, maintenance, permits and taxes
angle: Full-service means they onboard new properties continuously and control the listing. One relationship is many shoots rather than one. They already handle permits, so the licensing conversation is their language.

scale_note: Airbnb and vacation STR management; handles inquiries, bookings, cleaning, maintenance
angle: Same reseller logic. Lead with turnaround — 24 to 72 hours matters to a manager onboarding a property against an owner's revenue expectations.

Best multifamily fit on the list. Large enough that portfolio consistency is a real problem, small enough to reach a decision maker. 45 communities is the $850 property package repeated, or the $1,600/mo retainer.

scale_note: $500M+ in single-family, multi-family and commercial assets in and around Austin
angle: Austin-focused with a mixed portfolio, so they need both the per-unit and per-property scopes. Mixed asset types make one consistent shooter more valuable, not less.

scale_note: $200M+ assets under management; residential and multifamily
angle: Publishes its own comparison content on Austin property management, so they think about how they present. Receptive to a consistency argument.
Dedicated multifamily page — they market that specialism, so amenity and model-unit coverage lands.
Local operator. Lower ceiling than AMP but a shorter path to a yes.

scale_note: 22,000+ units under management; scattered-site portfolios through luxury high-rises
angle: Largest by unit count but multi-market and likely to have procurement between you and the decision. High ceiling, long cycle. Worth one attempt, not a campaign.

scale_note: National firm with an Austin office serving luxury multifamily
angle: National vendor-onboarding process. Realistically a form submission into a procurement queue. Lowest expected value per hour spent.
